body.statement:
Fix \(k\geq1\) and rational \(\varepsilon>0\), and define
\[
 \mathcal E_{k,\varepsilon}
 =\frac{4\int_{\mathbb R}|(\varphi_k^\dagger)'|^2
 +(5/8)\int_{\mathbb R}|x|(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2}
 {\int_{\mathbb R}(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2}
 +\frac{15}{256}\varepsilon.
\]
For every rational \(\eta>0\), a terminating rational calculation returns an integer \(N(k,\varepsilon,\eta)\) such that, whenever \(n\geq N(k,\varepsilon,\eta)\),
\[
 \alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\leq1,
 \qquad
 \max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
 G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
 \leq\mathcal E_{k,\varepsilon}+\eta.
 \tag{8}
\]
Moreover, if \(r_n/n=q^\dagger+n^{-1/6}u_n\), \(\mathbf1^\top u_n=0\), and \(u_n\to u\), then
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r_n)
 \leq\mathcal E_{k,\varepsilon}
 -2\sum_{a=1}^3\frac{u_a^2}{|c_a^\dagger|}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Thus the local design saddle is at \(q^\dagger\); after \(k\to\infty\) and then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), its coefficient is \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\).  The calculation covers positive exterior counts and every zero-count face, and its threshold is effective from the verified rational spline record.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(\alpha=n^{-1/3}\), \(q=r/n\), and
\[
 H(q)=\frac14\sum_{a=1}^3\frac{(c_a^\dagger)^2}{q_a}
 \tag{10}
\]
when every \(q_a>0\).  Since \(q_a^\dagger=|c_a^\dagger|/2\), Cauchy--Schwarz and direct expansion give the exact identities
\[
 H(q)\geq1,
 \qquad
 H(q)-1=\sum_{a=1}^3\frac{(q_a-q_a^\dagger)^2}{q_a}.
 \tag{11}
\]
Conditional on the prior coordinates, the cancellation of multinomial and orbit factors in the orbit lemma shows that the labeled response types are independent.  A unit observed in arm \(a\) is Bernoulli with mean
\[
 p_a(z)=\frac12+\alpha z_a,
 \qquad z=xv+hd^\dagger+\zeta\mathbf1,                 \tag{12}
\]
by (1).  Let \(P=\alpha x\) and let
\(H_n=n^{-1}\sum_i\theta_{t_i}\), which is the exact finite-population target.  No prior mean is substituted for \(H_n\).

We first lower-bound the Bayes risk for \(P\).  For positive \(q\), put
\[
 d_a(q)=\frac{c_a^\dagger}{4q_aH(q)}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Then \((c^\dagger)^\top d(q)=1\) and
\[
 \sum_aq_ad_a(q)^2=\frac1{4H(q)},
 \qquad
 |d_a(q)|\leq|c_a^\dagger|^{-1}.                       \tag{14}
\]
The three vectors \(v,d^\dagger,\mathbf1\) form a basis, so uniquely
\(d(q)=v+\beta(q)d^\dagger+\gamma(q)\mathbf1\).  The coefficient of \(v\) is one because the other two basis vectors are orthogonal to \(c^\dagger\).  If \(I_k=4\int| (\varphi_k^\dagger)'|^2/\int(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2\), the directional Fisher information of the product prior density is exactly
\[
 J(q)=I_k+\frac{10}{\varepsilon^2}
 \{\beta(q)^2+\gamma(q)^2\}.                           \tag{15}
\]
Indeed, the three coordinate scores have mean zero, their cross products integrate to zero under the product density, the longitudinal information is \(I_k\), and direct integration of \(\rho_\varepsilon\) gives
\[
 \int_{-\varepsilon}^{\varepsilon}
 \frac{\rho_\varepsilon'(s)^2}{\rho_\varepsilon(s)},ds
 =\frac{10}{\varepsilon^2}.                            \tag{16}
\]
The bound in (14) and the fixed inverse of the displayed rational basis give a finite, explicitly rationally bounded constant \(J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max}\) with \(J(q)\leq J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max}\) for every positive \(q\).

We derive, rather than assume, the information inequality used below.  Let \(\Pi\) denote the product prior density in the coordinates \((x,h,\zeta)\), and let \(L_z(o)\) be the Bernoulli likelihood from (12).  The amplitudes generating all three factors vanish on the boundary of their compact supports.  Weak integration by parts in direction \(d(q)\), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz, gives for every estimator \(D(o)\)
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \alpha
 &=\mathbb E[(D-P)\{\partial_{d(q)}\log\Pi
                  +\partial_{d(q)}\log L_z(O)\}],\\
 \mathbb E(D-P)^2
 &\geq\frac{\alpha^2}{J(q)+I_O(q)}.
 \end{aligned}                                         \tag{17}
\]
The cross term between the prior score and the likelihood score is zero because the latter has conditional mean zero.  If the compact support of \(z\) is bounded by \(Z_{k,\varepsilon}\) in maximum norm and \(2\alpha Z_{k,\varepsilon}<1\), (12)--(14) give
\[
 I_O(q)
 =\sum_a r_a\frac{\alpha^2d_a(q)^2}
 {p_a(z)\{1-p_a(z)\}}
 \leq\frac{n\alpha^2}{H(q)}L_n,
 \quad
 L_n=\{1-4\alpha^2Z_{k,\varepsilon}^2\}^{-1}.          \tag{18}
\]
Consequently the posterior-mean Bayes risk \(B_P(q)\) for \(P\) satisfies
\[
 B_P(q)\geq
 \frac{H(q)}{n\{L_n+J(q)H(q)n^{-1/3}\}}.              \tag{19}
\]

We next transfer (19) to the realized causal target.  For positive \(q\), define the observable Horvitz--Thompson average
\[
 \overline T=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
 \frac{c_{A_i}^\dagger(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1/2)}{q_{A_i}}.
\]
Conditional on \(z\), \(\mathbb E\overline T=P\) and
\(\mathbb E(\overline T-P)^2\leq H(q)/n\).  If
\(\mu=\mathbb E(P\mid O)\), posterior orthogonality yields
\[
 S(q):=\mathbb E(\overline T-\mu)^2
 =\mathbb E(\overline T-P)^2-B_P(q)
 \leq\frac{H(q)}n
 \frac{L_n-1+J(q)H(q)n^{-1/3}}
 {L_n+J(q)H(q)n^{-1/3}}.                               \tag{20}
\]
Put \(W_n=H_n-P\) and \(\zeta_O=\mathbb E(H_n\mid O)\).  The finite response alphabet, (1), compact support, and the lower bound
\(p_a(z),1-p_a(z)\geq1/4\) imply an explicit rational constant
\(C_{k,\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
 \left|\mathbb E(\theta_t-P\mid z,A_i=a,Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=y)\right|
 \leq C_{k,\varepsilon}\alpha.                        \tag{21}
\]
One may compute the least such displayed bound by enumerating the eight types, the six arm--outcome pairs, and the finitely many sign cells.  Conditional independence and the fact that each conditional summand in (21) has mean zero give
\[
 D(q):=\mathbb E(\zeta_O-\mu)^2
 \leq C_{k,\varepsilon}^2\frac{\alpha^2}{n}.           \tag{22}
\]
The moment identities (1) give exactly
\[
 \mathbb EW_n^2
 =\frac1n\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(\theta_t\mid x,h,\zeta)
 \leq n^{-4/3}\overline V_{k,\varepsilon},
 \quad
 \overline V_{k,\varepsilon}
 =\frac58\int|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
  +\frac{15}{256}\varepsilon.                          \tag{23}
\]
The coefficient \(15/256\) uses
\(\int|h|\rho_\varepsilon(h)\,dh=5\varepsilon/16\).

There is also an exact covariance identity.  Since
\(\sum_ac_a^\dagger(t_a-1/2)=\theta_t\), independence across units and the fixed arm counts imply
\[
 \mathbb E\{(P-\overline T)W_n\mid z\}
 =-\mathbb E(W_n^2\mid z).                              \tag{24}
\]
Expanding around \(\mu\), using
\(\mathbb E[(\overline T-\mu)W_n]
 =\mathbb E[(\overline T-\mu)(\zeta_O-\mu)]\), and completing the posterior square gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E(H_n-\zeta_O)^2
 &=B_P(q)-\mathbb EW_n^2
   +2\mathbb E[(\overline T-\mu)(\zeta_O-\mu)]-D(q)\\
 &\geq B_P(q)-\mathbb EW_n^2-2\sqrt{S(q)D(q)}-D(q).
 \end{aligned}                                         \tag{25}
\]
Every term in (25) concerns the realized finite-population target.

Let \(a_n=n^{1/3}\) and
\(D_n(q)=L_n+J(q)H(q)/a_n\).  Equations (19)--(25) yield the explicit computable envelope
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
 \leq{}&a_n\left\{1-\frac{H(q)}{D_n(q)}\right\}
 +\overline V_{k,\varepsilon}\\
 &+2C_{k,\varepsilon}
 \left[
 \frac{H(q)\{D_n(q)-1\}}{D_n(q)}
 \right]^{1/2}
 +\frac{C_{k,\varepsilon}^2}{a_n}.
\end{aligned}                                          \tag{26}
\]

We now maximize this envelope without omitting allocation faces.  On the local set in the theorem statement, (11) gives
\(H(q)-1=O(n^{-11/36})\).  Equations (13)--(15) then give
\[
 \beta(q)^2+\gamma(q)^2=O(n^{-11/36}),
 \qquad J(q)=I_k+O_{k,\varepsilon}(n^{-11/36}).         \tag{27}
\]
Also \(a_n(L_n-1)=O_{k,\varepsilon}(n^{-1/3})\).  Substitution in (26) shows, uniformly on the local set,
\[
 G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
 \leq I_k+\overline V_{k,\varepsilon}+o_{k,\varepsilon}(1)
 =\mathcal E_{k,\varepsilon}+o_{k,\varepsilon}(1).    \tag{28}
\]
If the sharper local parameterization in (9) holds, (11) gives
\[
 a_n\{H(q)-1\}\longrightarrow
 2\sum_a\frac{u_a^2}{|c_a^\dagger|},                  \tag{29}
\]
while all other limits in (27)--(28) are unchanged.  Keeping the negative term in the first line of (26) proves (9).  This independently verifies that the local maximizer is \(q^\dagger\).

For completeness, consider the positive-count exterior.  Its definition and (11) imply
\[
 a_n\{H(q)-1\}\geq n^{1/36}.                          \tag{30}
\]
For fixed \((k,\varepsilon)\), the constants in (26) are finite.  If
\(H(q)\leq a_n/(2J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max})\), then
\(D_n(q)\leq2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  On \(1\leq H\leq2\), (30) inserted directly in (26) sends its right side to \(-\infty\).  On \(2\leq H\leq4\), one has \(D_n(q)-H\leq-1/4\) eventually, so the first term in (26) is at most \(-a_n/8\).  On \(4\leq H\leq a_n/(2J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max})\), one has \(D_n(q)-H\leq-H/4\), so that term is at most \(-a_nH/8\).  In both subranges the square-root term is
\(O_{k,\varepsilon}(\sqrt H+H/\sqrt{a_n})\), and is dominated by the displayed negative bound.  These are comparisons of explicit rational powers.

If \(H(q)>a_n/(2J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max})\), use (19) and the monotonicity of \(H/(L_n+J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max}H/a_n)\) to obtain
\[
 B_P(q)\geq\frac{a_n}{4J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max}n}     \tag{31}
\]
eventually.  The \(L^2\) triangle inequality between \(H_n\), \(P\), and an arbitrary data action, together with (23), gives
\[
 \{mathbb E(H_n-D)^2\}^{1/2}
 \geq \sqrt{B_P(q)}-sqrt{\mathbb EW_n^2}.
\]
Equations (23) and (31) imply a lower bound of order
\(n^{-2/3}/J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max}\), which is strictly larger than \(n^{-1}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Thus the exterior maximum of \(G\) is eventually below the right side of (8).

Finally suppose at least one arm count is zero, and let \(F\) be the set of observed arms.  Choose a two-arm face containing \(F\), and use its direction in (2).  Its observed Bernoulli likelihood is constant along that direction by (6), its target derivative is one, and its product-prior directional information is a finite explicitly rationally bounded number \(J_F\).  The integration-by-parts argument (17), now with zero likelihood information, gives
\[
 B_P(q)\geq\alpha^2/J_F.                               \tag{32}
\]
Combining (32), (23), and the same \(L^2\) triangle inequality gives Bayes risk of order \(n^{-2/3}/J_F\), again strictly larger than \(n^{-1}\).  This proves the zero-face part.

All constants just used are obtained by rational matrix inversion, finite type and sign-cell enumeration, and exact integration of the verified rational splines and polynomial transverse density.  The inequalities after (26) involve only rational constants and ordered algebraic powers of \(n\).  Enumerating \(n\) until their monotone upper bounds are below \(\eta\) therefore terminates and returns \(N(k,\varepsilon,\eta)\).  Equations (28), (30)--(32) prove (8) with that effective threshold.  Finally, the effective Airy-record lemma gives
\[
 \frac{4\int| (\varphi_k^\dagger)'|^2
 +(5/8)\int|x|(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2}
 {\int(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2}
 \leq\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+2^{-k},
\]
so sending \(k\to\infty\) and \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) in the local saddle yields \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\), as claimed.
body.justification: This is the load-bearing finite-to-limit bridge: it derives one computable Bayes envelope for every allocation count and the local Airy saddle.
body.gap: Its effective constants are pointwise in the fixed spline record and transverse width, which is sufficient for the certified diagonal.
body.consumer: Consumed directly by the allocation-tube theorem.
